title: Degree Sequences vs. Forests in Finite Graphs
summary: We prove two conjectures of Shteiner and Shteyner stating that for an undirected graph $G=(V,E)$, the number of degree sequences arising from its spanning subgraphs is at least the number of forests in $G$, with equality if and only if $G$ is bipartite. In the process of proving the bipartite case, we provide several equivalent evaluations of the Tutte polynomial $T_G(x,y)$ at $(2,1)$, including interpretations in terms of degree vectors obtained from orientations of $G$.
